extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry; readers of Ravi Vakil's 'The Rising Sea'
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook chapter excerpt covering properties of coherent and quasicoherent sheaves (duals, support, rank, local freeness, torsion), coherence over non-Noetherian rings, and the theory of line bundles and Weil divisors on schemes (construction of O(n), divisors, OX(D), and the div map).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duals of coherent sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming OX is coherent, if F is coherent then its dual F∨ := Hom(F, OX) is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes duals of vector bundles. There is a natural double dual morphism (F∨)∨ → F which need not be an isomorphism in general; coherent sheaves for which this double-dual morphism is an isomorphism are called reflexive. Example: for the coherent sheaf associated to k[t]/(t) on A1 = Spec k[t], one has F∨ = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom(F, G) for finite-rank locally free F
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finite rank locally free and G is quasicoherent, then Hom(F, G) ≅ F∨ ⊗ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holds more generally if G is any O-module; exercise asks to describe an isomorphism using trivializations of F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dualizing exact sequences with locally free term
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an exact sequence 0 → F → G → H → 0 of quasicoherent sheaves with H locally free, for any quasicoherent E the sequence 0 → Hom(H, E) → Hom(G, E) → Hom(F, E) → 0 is exact (i.e., Hom(–,E) is exact on the left and becomes exact on the right in this situation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uses left-exactness of Hom and the fact that locally (affine, with H ≅ A^⊕n) the short exact sequence splits so dualizing preserves exactness. In particular, if F,G,H,OX coherent and H locally free, then 0 → H∨ → G∨ → F∨ → 0 is exact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of a finite type quasicoherent sheaf is closed
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on a scheme X, then Supp F is a closed subset of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: reduce to the affine case and use a finite set of generators of the corresponding module. Warning: the support of a general quasicoherent sheaf need not be closed (counterexamples given). On a locally Noetherian scheme the sheaf of nilpotents is coherent and hence has closed support; the reduced locus is open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric Nakayama (generation of fiber implies generation nearby)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a scheme and F a finite type quasicoherent sheaf, and sections a1,...,an ∈ F(U) have images generating the fiber F|p at p, then there exists an affine neighborhood Spec A of p where the sections generate F(Spec A) as an A-module, generically generate stalks F_q, and their fibers generate F|q for q in Spec A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exercise spells out three senses of 'generate' (global on Spec A, at all stalks, and on fibers). Use Nakayama-type arguments locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local freeness of finitely presented sheaf is stalk-local
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finitely presented on X and F_p is a free O_{X,p}-module for some p, then F is locally free in some open neighborhood of p. Hence F is locally free iff every stalk F_p is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Geometric Nakayama to lift generators from the fiber to a neighborhood and analyze the kernel (finite type with closed support) to show the surjection becomes an isomorphism off a closed set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion/torsion-free structure on regular curves
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Torsion-free coherent sheaves on a regular (locally Noetherian) curve are locally free. (b) Torsion coherent sheaves on a quasicompact regular integral curve are supported at finitely many closed points. (c) For a coherent sheaf F on a quasicompact regular curve, there is a canonical short exact sequence 0 → F_tor → F → F_lf → 0 with F_tor torsion and F_lf locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to discrete valuation ring case and use the PID structure theorem for finitely generated modules: summands are of form A or A/m^k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modules over DVR: torsion-free iff free (finite gen)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a finitely generated module over a discrete valuation ring, then M is torsion-free iff M is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition highlights necessity of finite generation; without it or without dimension-1 or regular hypotheses, the statement can fail (counterexamples offered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of rank at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasicoherent sheaf F on X and point p, the fiber F|p := F_p ⊗_{O_{X,p}} κ(p) and rank at p is dim_{κ(p)} F_p/mF_p (possibly infinite). This agrees with locally free rank when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On affine Spec A with module M, rank is dim_{K(A/p)} M_p/pM_p. For finite type sheaves rank at p is finite and equals the minimal number of generators of M_p. Rank behaves well under direct sums, tensor products, quotients, and localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank commutes with sums, tensors, and quotients/localizations
rubrics_metrics.description: At any point, rank(F ⊕ G) = rank F + rank G and rank(F ⊗ G) = rank F · rank G; rank commutes with ring quotients and localizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: show M ⊗_R (R/I) ≅ M/IM, and use basic module algebra to check equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semicontinuity of rank for finite type sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on X, then the function rank(F) is upper semicontinuous on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof hint: generators at a point are generators nearby by Geometric Nakayama; the finiteness hypothesis is necessary (counterexample earlier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant rank on reduced scheme implies local freeness
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is reduced and F a finite type quasicoherent sheaf with constant rank n, then F is locally free of rank n. Consequently, on an integral scheme finite type sheaves are locally free on a dense open set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to the affine case and use Geometric Nakayama to lift a basis of the fiber; reducedness ensures certain coefficients cannot be nilpotent and become invertible in local rings. Counterexamples exist when X is not reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a finite morphism at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite morphism π: X → Y, the sheaf π_* O_X is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on Y, and the rank of this sheaf at point p is called the degree of π at p. The degree is an upper semicontinuous function on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree can jump (e.g., closed embedding of point into line), or be constant in surprising ways. Exercise: degree at p equals dimension of functions on scheme-theoretic preimage π^{-1}(p) over κ(p); degree zero iff fiber empty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence implications: coherent ⇒ finitely presented ⇒ finitely generated
rubrics_metrics.description: For modules over a ring A, coherent implies finitely presented which implies finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was discussed earlier in the text; exercises illustrate the relations and converse failures in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero module is coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: The zero module (0) is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trivial check; included as a basic closure property for the class of coherent modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-exactness: N finitely generated implies P finitely generated
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → M → N → P → 0 exact, if N is finitely generated then P is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses surjectivity onto P; only right-exactness needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-generation propagation: M,P finitely generated imply N finitely generated
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → M → N → P → 0 exact, if M and P are finitely generated then N is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only right-exactness of the sequence is needed; exercise suggests a constructive approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure example: N,P finitely generated need not imply M finitely generated
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist exact sequences 0 → M → N → P → 0 with N and P finitely generated but M not finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise gives hint using quotient A/I and a short exact sequence 0 → I → A → A/I → 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness consequence: if N coherent and M finitely generated then M coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: In an exact sequence 0 → M → N → P → 0, if N is coherent and M is finitely generated then M is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only left-exactness of the sequence is required; follow coherence definition checking finite generation of kernels of maps from finite free modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: If N and P coherent then M coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → M → N → P → 0 and N, P coherent, then M is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the definition of coherence and diagram chases (hint: write presentations by finite free modules and apply Snake Lemma).

rubrics_metrics.name: If M finitely generated and N coherent then P coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: In 0 → M → N → P → 0, if M is finitely generated and N is coherent then P is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Left-exactness is sufficient for the argument; see exercise hints in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: If M and P coherent then N coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: In 0 → M → N → P → 0, if M and P are coherent then N is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard closure property of the class of coherent modules; exercise provides hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite direct sums of coherent modules are coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite direct sum of coherent A-modules is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Straightforward property needed to establish that coherent modules form an abelian category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of map from finitely generated to coherent is coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated, N coherent, and φ: M → N any map, then Im φ is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that images of maps from finite free modules into coherent modules are coherent; exercise gives details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernels and cokernels of maps between coherent modules are coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: For maps of coherent modules, both kernel and cokernel are coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of checking the category of coherent modules is abelian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum and intersection of coherent submodules are coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If M and N are coherent submodules of a coherent module P, then M + N and M ∩ N are coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: consider the natural maps to P and use closure under images and kernels.

rubrics_metrics.name: If A is coherent then finitely presented modules are coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ring A is coherent (as an A-module), then every finitely presented A-module is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, if finitely presented modules are coherent then A is coherent since A is finitely presented over itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom of finitely presented into coherent is coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely presented and N is coherent then Hom(M, N) is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use left-exactness of Hom in the first argument and finite presentation to control kernels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensoring finitely presented with coherent yields coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely presented and N is coherent then M ⊗_A N is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presentation of M and exactness properties of tensor product (exercise points to left-exactness and presentations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves finite generation/presentation/coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ A, and M is finitely generated (resp. finitely presented, coherent) as an A-module, then M_f is finitely generated (resp. finitely presented, coherent) as an A_f-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exactness of localization; exercise repeats an earlier one to keep section self-contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing criterion for finite generation: cover by D(fi)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (f1,...,fn)=A and M_fi is finitely generated for all i, then M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct generators locally and check surjectivity on the distinguished opens D(fi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing criterion for coherence: cover by D(fi)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (f1,...,fn)=A and M_fi is coherent for all i, then M is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check finite generation of kernels locally and apply previous exercises to deduce global coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent modules form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: The class of coherent modules is closed under 0, finite sums, kernels, cokernels, images, and hence forms an abelian subcategory of A-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises in this section verify each closure property (0 in set, closed under sums, kernels, cokernels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of O(n) on projective space via transition functions
rubrics_metrics.description: On P^m_k the invertible sheaf O(n) is defined by trivializations on the standard affine cover U_i with transition functions x_{i/j}^n = x_j/i^{-n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition functions satisfy cocycle condition; O(n)⊗O(m)=O(n+m); O(-n) is the dual of O(n). On P^1, O(1) trivializes on U0 and U1 with transition x0/1 = x1/0^{-1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global sections of O(n) identified with homogeneous polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections of O(n) on P^m_k are naturally identified with homogeneous degree-n polynomials in the m+1 variables; in particular dim_k Γ(P^1, O(n)) = n+1 for n ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the explicit transition functions and compatibility on overlaps. For n ≥ 0 cohomology vanishing in higher degree yields Euler characteristic equals h^0; later the polynomial behavior in n is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification needed for tensor product global sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Global sections do not commute with tensor product of sheaves in general: (F ⊗ G)(X) need not equal F(X) ⊗_{O_X(X)} G(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: on P^1_k, F = O(1) and G = O(-1) give O(1)⊗O(-1) ≅ O but O(1)(P^1) ⊗ O(-1)(P^1) = (2-dim space) ⊗ 0 = 0, so the global sections tensor does not recover global sections of the tensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification on P^1: all invertible sheaves are O(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every invertible sheaf on P^1_k is isomorphic to O(n) for some integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use classification of finitely generated modules over a PID to show invertible sheaves on A^1 are trivial and analyze transition functions on the standard cover of P^1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Weil divisors
rubrics_metrics.description: A Weil divisor on a Noetherian scheme X is a formal Z-linear combination ∑ n_Y [Y] of codimension-1 irreducible closed subsets Y, with all but finitely many n_Y = 0. Support and effectiveness are defined in the obvious way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On curves Weil divisors are linear combinations of closed points. One may restrict divisors to opens and consider principal and locally principal divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisor of a rational section of a line bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is invertible and s is a rational section not identically vanishing on any component, then div(s) := ∑_Y val_Y(s) [Y], summing over codimension-1 irreducible Y; val_Y(s) computed using a local trivialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: val_Y(s) is well-defined since different trivializations differ by invertible functions; only finitely many Y contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Div map from (L, s) pairs to Weil divisors and injectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignment (L, s) ↦ div(s) defines a group homomorphism from isomorphism classes of pairs (invertible sheaf, nonzero rational section) to Weil(X). If X is normal and Noetherian then this map is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injectivity: if div(L,s)=0 then s has no poles and is regular; then s gives an isomorphism O_X → L on trivializing opens since s corresponds to an invertible function locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of O_X(D) for a Weil divisor D
rubrics_metrics.description: For irreducible normal X and Weil divisor D, define O_X(D)(U) := { t ∈ K(X)× : div|_U(t) + D|_U ≥ 0 } ∪ {0}; these are rational functions whose zeros/poles are constrained by D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OX(D) comes equipped with a canonical rational section corresponding to 1 ∈ K(X)×; away from Supp D this sheaf is isomorphic to O_X (Algebraic Hartogs). Verify quasicoherence using distinguished affine criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: OX(D) invertible ⇔ D locally principal
rubrics_metrics.description: If D is locally principal then O_X(D) is locally isomorphic to O_X and hence an invertible sheaf; conversely, if O_X(D) is invertible then D is locally principal (exercise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation: if D is principal then O_X(D) ≅ O_X. Exercise 14.2.E constructs an explicit isomorphism O(div s) ≅ L for L invertible and s a rational section, and 14.2.G addresses the converse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction isomorphism O(div s) ≅ L for a rational section s
rubrics_metrics.description: Given invertible sheaf L and nonzero rational section s, there is an isomorphism O_X(div(s)) ≅ L (uses normality hypothesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build local isomorphisms on opens where O(div s) and L are trivial using multiplication by s; check these glue to a sheaf isomorphism and that σ(1)=s under the chosen identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example of Weil divisor not locally principal (cone)
rubrics_metrics.description: On X = Spec k[x,y,z]/(xy − z^2) (a cone) the divisor D given by z = x = 0 is not locally principal; in particular O_X(D) is not invertible. Also div(x) = 2D (the plane x=0 is tangent to the cone along D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses analysis at the origin/stalks and Zariski tangent space; illustrates that O_X(D) need not be invertible in non-factorial/non-normal situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: If X is Noetherian factorial then O(D) invertible for any Weil divisor D
rubrics_metrics.description: On a Noetherian factorial scheme X, for any Weil divisor D the sheaf O_X(D) is an invertible sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to irreducible components and cover X by opens where the prime defining each codimension-1 Y is principal (UFD property). Construct local generators f with div(f) = [Y] on each open and remove other zeros/poles.
